evidence.label: Every complex K3 surface is Oka

headline: A claimed proof that every complex K3 surface is Oka: local holomorphic maps into it can be copied by entire maps.
scope: It covers every complex K3 surface, projective or not; the class VII claim covers minimal surfaces only.
plain: An Oka space is one where a holomorphic map defined near a small convex set can be copied by a map defined everywhere. K3 surfaces are compact complex surfaces with a special two-form, and many contain no curves. Earlier work showed the property for special K3 surfaces and for a dense set of them. This paper claims it for every complex K3 surface. No computer has checked the proof.
doesNot: This does not cover blown-up surfaces or properly elliptic surfaces in its classification.
origin: This result comes from an unreleased OpenAI model, published in the openai/math release on 6 October 2026.

scorecard.firstStepBy: Buzzard and Lu, dominability of elliptic and Kummer K3 surfaces
scorecard.significanceWhy: If the proof holds, it answers a named problem in Oka theory for a central class of complex surfaces.

explanation:
Take the function 1/(1 − z) on the disc of complex numbers z with size at most 1/2. Add up the polynomial 1 + z + z² + … + z¹⁰. On that disc, the polynomial differs from the function by at most (1/2)¹⁰, which is 1/1024. A polynomial is defined on the whole complex plane, not just the disc. So a map defined near a small set has been copied, almost exactly, by a map defined everywhere. Maps that are complex-differentiable are called holomorphic. Maps defined on the whole of ℂᵐ are called entire.

Now change the target. Ask for entire maps into the unit disc, instead of into the plane. A classical theorem of Liouville says every bounded entire function is constant. So no entire map can copy the identity map of a small disc. The disc is too rigid for this game. A target space is called Oka when the game always works. Take any holomorphic map from near a compact convex set in ℂᵐ, in any dimension m. Entire maps must copy it as closely as one likes. Forstnerič proved that this convex approximation property characterizes Oka manifolds[3].

A K3 surface is a compact complex surface where every loop can shrink to a point. It carries a nowhere-zero holomorphic two-form[1]. That form measures small complex areas. K3 surfaces have a rigid topology, but many have very few curves. A K3 surface need not be projective, meaning it may not fit inside any projective space defined by polynomial equations. It may contain no curves at all[2]. That makes them a natural test for flexibility.

Partial results built up over 25 years. Buzzard and Lu showed in 2000 that elliptic and Kummer K3 surfaces receive maps from ℂ² that cover open sets[4]. Kamenova, Lu and Verbitsky showed in 2014 that a certain distance, the Kobayashi pseudodistance, is zero on every K3 surface[5]. That removed one obstruction but gave no approximation[6]. Alarcón and Forstnerič proved a one-dimensional version, Oka-1, for Kummer and elliptic K3 surfaces[7]. Xie and Zhao showed in 2026 that Oka K3 surfaces are dense among all K3 surfaces[8]. Dense is not all, though. A dense set of good surfaces does not settle each surface[9].

This paper claims to prove that every complex K3 surface is Oka[10]. That includes surfaces with no curves, with no condition on special fibrations[11]. One consequence is a single entire curve that passes through any chosen point with any chosen nonzero velocity. Its image comes as close as one likes to every point of the surface[14]. The paper also claims that every minimal compact complex surface of Kodaira dimension zero is Oka[15]. Here minimal means no part can be blown down. Kodaira dimension zero means its special forms neither vanish nor multiply. For class VII surfaces, a further family, it claims Oka holds exactly for Hopf and Enoki surfaces. That part depends on a separate OpenAI manuscript, not on the K3 argument[16].

The main obstacle is building maps on a surface that may have no curves to work with. On projective K3 surfaces, families of genus-one curves supply flows that run for all complex time[13]. On the others, the paper builds long chains of thin annular pieces. Annuli are ring-shaped regions. Small errors at each join must be fixed without the chain growing thin[12]. The paper then uses the dynamics of K3 periods to carry the property to every surface. A period is a plane in a fixed lattice that records the two-form.

How sure is this? No Lean formalization is listed for this result. The argument combines complex analysis, period dynamics and earlier deep theorems. No specialist review has been published.
hypeCheck: No Lean check is listed. The proof is long and analytic, the class VII part leans on another unreviewed manuscript, and no specialist review is published.

glossary.meaning: A map between complex spaces that is complex-differentiable.
A holomorphic map defined on the whole of ℂᵐ.
A complex space where maps from near a compact convex set can always be approximated by entire maps.
A compact, simply connected complex surface with a nowhere-zero holomorphic two-form.
Fitting inside a projective space as the zero set of polynomial equations.
A measure of how fast special forms on a shape multiply; zero means they stay constant.
The plane in a fixed lattice that records a K3 surface's holomorphic two-form.

claims.text: Chen and Gounelas families of genus-one curves supply flows on projective K3 surfaces.
claims.sourceQuote: Their complete genus-one fibers supply holomorphic flows for all complex times, and the difference in degrees forces their tangent directions to be generically independent.

claims.text: Every K3 surface has a dense entire curve with prescribed point and tangent vector.
claims.sourceQuote: For every $x\in S$ and every nonzero vector $v\in T_xS$, there is a holomorphic immersion $f:\C\to S$ such that \[ f(0)=x,\qquad f'(0)=v,\qquad \overline{f(\C)}=S, \] where closure is taken in the ordinary complex topology.

claims.text: Every minimal compact complex surface of Kodaira dimension zero is Oka.
claims.sourceQuote: More generally, every connected minimal compact complex surface of Kodaira dimension zero is Oka.
